extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers, state regulators, utilities, FERC, and energy industry stakeholders (including electric cooperatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Public comments (NRECA) critiquing EPA's Proposed Clean Power Plan (111(d)) targets and the technical, legal, and factual bases (the "Building Blocks") used to set state targets, with emphasis on reliability, infrastructure, and data/analysis validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for natural gas availability assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA cannot simply assume the availability (or planned future availability) of sufficient natural gas generation, natural gas pipeline capacity, or natural gas storage to support EPA’s proposed environmental dispatch, particularly in ISO/RTO markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain and provide evidence for the availability and deliverability of gas-fired generation (including pipeline capacity and nearby high-capacity storage), especially during peak/winter periods and extreme weather events (e.g., the Polar Vortex). Discuss instances where firm transportation was curtailed despite contracts and where units were unable to procure gas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for winter/peak constraints on firm gas transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm transportation service is not always available in the winter, and purchasing firm transportation service for gas is often not economically feasible when that service is only needed during extreme weather events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe economic and physical limits on acquiring firm pipeline capacity for generators, and include evidence (e.g., events where cooperatives with firm service experienced curtailment or no deliverability) showing that contracted firm service does not guarantee delivery during peaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider gas-electric operational differences and scheduling misalignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in the operational structure of the natural gas and electricity markets (scheduling timelines, nomination processes, intra-day nomination opportunities) make it difficult for gas-fired generation to obtain fuel when dispatch changes are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze scheduling discontinuities (operating day differences, lack of synchronization between day-ahead nomination and day-ahead electric market scheduling, limited intraday nomination) and how they impede reliability under increased reliance on gas generation; reference FERC findings and ongoing rulemakings addressing these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate whether increased gas generation can be reliably used
rubrics_metrics.description: There is concern that steps must be taken to ensure that ever-increasing amounts of gas generation can be used to serve load reliably; EPA should not assume reliability without addressing these steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete measures, timeline, and evidence showing how gas scheduling, pipeline operations, and delivery constraints will be resolved to support the proposed dispatch levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for pipeline development incentives and anchor-customer assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Rule assumes necessary gas distribution infrastructure exists or will be built, but gas pipeline developers are reluctant to build pipelines without 'anchor' customers; generation owners will not commit to long-term contracts without dispatch certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the Rule creates credible demand signals or contractual certainty for pipeline developers; address the circular problem where infrastructure requires anchor customers but generators require dispatch certainty to commit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume renewables are fully integrated or available everywhere
rubrics_metrics.description: The environmental dispatch will increase reliance on renewable generation, but FERC integration efforts are in preliminary stages and unresolved operational/commercial issues remain that could impact reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the current status of renewable interconnection, scheduling, ancillary services, and any regional limitations; do not assume uniform nationwide readiness for high renewable penetration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect FERC jurisdiction and existing tariffs when prescribing environmental dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: States cannot lawfully implement an environmental dispatch that conflicts with FERC tariffs, whether in organized markets or other FERC-jurisdictional services; therefore FERC must control how renewable resources may be used to implement the environmental dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential conflicts between state-level dispatch directives and FERC OATT/market rules; coordinate with FERC and account for tariffed transmission rights and market rules in any proposed dispatch mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for transmission rights and first-in-time priority under the OATT
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Rule’s environmental dispatch may be inconsistent with FERC’s Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) first-in-time priority to transmission capacity (Designated Network Resources and long-term firm transmission service), potentially interfering with transmission reservation and requiring significant transmission expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how shifting dispatch priorities would interact with queued transmission service requests, network resource designations, and utilities' rights under Section 217 of the FPA; include cost and timing estimates for any required transmission expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not finalize Building Block targets without record support
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s Building Block assumptions regarding legal applicability, technical capability, and related factual assumptions are unfounded, inexpert, and arbitrary – making the Building Blocks fatally flawed unless supported by the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical, technical, and legal evidence for each Building Block assumption; avoid relying on speculative or generalized projections without unit- or system-level data support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow adjustments if Building Blocks prove incorrect
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assumes that a State failing to achieve reductions in one Building Block can compensate by increasing utilization of other Blocks, but the record contains no support for this and EPA makes no provision for adjusting overall state targets if a Building Block assumption is wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanisms in the rulemaking for revising state targets or providing flexibility if particular Building Block potentials are later determined infeasible in a State or region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits to reductions from each Building Block
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of any State to use any particular Building Block is limited: heat-rate improvements are limited to a maximum of about 6 percent; end-user efficiency reductions limited to approximately 1.5 percent per year; re-dispatch to NGCC and renewables limited by capacity and infrastructure availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify realistic upper bounds for each Building Block per State, and do not assume unbounded substitutability between Blocks when setting targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require unit-by-unit analysis for Heat Rate Improvement (HRI) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to conclude that a 2 to 4% HRI through equipment upgrades is obtainable for any individual EGU or aggregation without conducting a unit-by-unit evaluation because units vary by design, prior upgrades, operational approaches, and load profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct detailed, site-specific technical assessments for each designated coal-fired EGU before assigning HRI obligations; do not generalize from conceptual or literature-based estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume HRI effects are additive across strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA appears to have treated HRI ranges as additive and universally applicable, but combinations of strategies do not always provide heat rate reductions equal to the sum of each individual strategy because many technologies affect interrelated plant variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model interaction effects among HRI strategies and require case-specific evaluations of combined measures rather than summing individual theoretical impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for degradation and impacts from pollution-control installations on HRI
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance of some HRI strategies degrades over time, and installation of additional pollution controls (regional haze rules, MATS) will decrease unit heat rate efficiency compared to pre-installation levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate maintenance degradation rates and the net heat-rate effect of required environmental control retrofits in HRI potential estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider regulatory constraints (e.g., New Source Review) on HRI options
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the options for HRI listed in the cited studies have triggered New Source Review actions by EPA and others, which may limit applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether particular HRI technologies or upgrades would trigger NSR or other permitting hurdles and factor those constraints into feasibility and cost analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and validate underlying studies before relying on them (S&L critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA misapplied the 2009 Sargent & Lundy report: the S&L report did not conclude that any individual or aggregated EGU can achieve the 6% HRI assumed by EPA; its case studies were conceptual and not based on detailed site-specific analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using third-party studies, confirm the scope and limitations of those studies, and obtain clarification from authors where necessary; do not extrapolate conceptual estimates to binding targets without verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor reporting methodology and data quality (CEMS issues) into HRI analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA itself found that approximately two-thirds of large decreases in reported heat rate can be associated with changes in reporting methods (CEMS) rather than actual efficiency improvements, but EPA failed to account for this in its matrix analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit CEMS data, investigate reporting method changes and instrument calibration events, and adjust analyses to remove artifacts due to measurement or reporting changes before attributing observed heat-rate changes to operational improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a rational, documented basis for any empirical assumptions in matrix analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA constructed a 168-bin matrix and arbitrarily assumed a 30% reduction of the difference to the 10th percentile to derive a 4% best-practice HRI without a technical rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply methodological justification, sensitivity analysis, and technical explanation for any arbitrary factors or thresholds used in statistical/matrix analyses; avoid unexplained calibration that yields convenient target numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact unit owners/operators to validate cause of observed HRIs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the sixteen-unit study EPA did not contact owners to determine actual causes for apparent heat rate reductions; industry investigation found reductions were almost exclusively due to CEMS reporting or calibration changes rather than true efficiency gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before concluding that observed improvements are meaningful and transferable, perform outreach/data verification with unit owners/operators and incorporate their input into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technically appropriate ambient temperature metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s use of ambient temperature as a contributor to heat-rate variation is questionable technically, depending on unit cooling systems and rate of temperature change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose ambient temperature metrics that reflect unit-specific thermodynamic relationships and cooling systems; validate regression attributions to avoid misassigning variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure HRI improvements are verifiable and meaningful at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Where improvement options are limited (e.g., to boiler island measures), the weighted average past and future HRI potential may be negligible (e.g., ~0.04% past, 0.08% future) and impossible to verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only adopt HRI assumptions that are practically verifiable on a unit/year basis and that would yield measurable system-level emission reductions; be skeptical of fleet-average figures that are below detection/verification thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reliability risks from increased gas-electric dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: As gas-electric dependency significantly increases, events like the 2014 Polar Vortex could disrupt natural gas supply and delivery for the power sector in high-congestion regions, increasing the risk for potential blackouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reliability risk assessments (probabilistic or scenario-based) that consider extreme weather, pipeline outages, fuel procurement difficulties, and cascading effects on generation dispatch and system security.
